source_text: Quanta autem Domini indulgentia, quanta circa nos dignationis eius et bonitatis ubertas, ut sic nos uoluerit orationem celebrare in conspectu Dei, ut Dominum patrem uocemus et ut est Christus Dei filius sic et nos Dei filii nuncupemur: quod nomen nemo nostrum in oratione auderet adtingere, nisi ipse nobis sic permisisset orare. meminisse itaque, fratres dilectissimi, et scire debemus quia quando patrem Deum dicimus quasi filii Dei agere debemus, ut quomodo nos nobis placemus de Deo patre, sic sibi placeat et ille de nobis. conuersemur quasi Dei templa, ut Dominum in nobis constet habitare. nec sit degener actus noster ab spiritu, ut qui spiritales et caelestes esse coepimus non nisi spiritalia et caelestia cogitemus et agamus, quia et ipse Dominus Deus dixit: eos qui clarificant me clarificabo: et qui me spernent spernentur, beatus quoque apostolus iii epistula sua posuit : non estis uestri, empti enim estis pretio magno. clarificate et portate Deum in corpore uestro.
thought_title: Living as children of the Father we name
orientation: Cyprian has explained calling God our Father and now draws out what that name requires of the reborn.
pass_a_gloss: But how great is the indulgence of the Lord, how great toward us is the abundance of his condescension and of his goodness, in that he has willed that we perform prayer in this way in the sight of God, that we call the Lord father and that as Christ is Son of God so also we be named children of God: which name none of us would dare to lay hold of in prayer, unless he himself had permitted us to pray in this way. Therefore, most beloved brothers, we ought to remember and to know that when we say God as father we ought to act as children of God, so that just as we are pleased for ourselves concerning God as father, so also he may be pleased for himself concerning us. Let us live as temples of God, so that it may be established that the Lord dwells in us. And let our action not be degenerate from the spirit, so that we who have begun to be spiritual and heavenly may think and do nothing except spiritual and heavenly things, because the Lord God himself also has said: those who glorify me I will glorify: and those who spurn me will be spurned, and the blessed apostle also has put in his letter: you are not your own, for you have been bought at a great price. Glorify and carry God in your body.

choices.why: marks God stooping to grant sinners the Father name, not general dignity
ubertas is fullness overflowing toward us, kept as quantity noun
celebrare is formal performance of worship, not festal celebrating

choices.english: let us live as temples of God
choices.why: hortatory subjunctive for conduct of life, matching temple indwelling clause

bible_refs.note: eos qui clarificant me clarificabo: et qui me spernent spernentur
non estis uestri, empti enim estis pretio magno. clarificate et portate Deum in corpore uestro

pass_b_english: How great is the Lord’s kindness, how great his condescension toward us and the abundance of his goodness! He willed us to perform prayer in God’s presence in this way. We call the Lord Father. As Christ is the Son of God, so we are named children of God. None of us would dare to take up that name in prayer, unless he himself had given us leave to pray like this.

So, dearest brothers, we must remember and know this. When we call God Father, we must act as children of God. As we delight in God as Father, so he must delight in us. Let us live as temples of God, so that it is plain the Lord dwells in us. Let no act of ours fall away from the Spirit. We have begun to be spiritual and heavenly, so let us think and do only what is spiritual and heavenly. For the Lord God himself has said: “Those who glorify me I will glorify, and those who despise me shall be despised” (1 Samuel 2:30). And the blessed apostle Paul has also set it down in his letter: “You are not your own, for you were bought at a great price. Glorify God and bear him in your body” (1 Corinthians 6:19-20).
notes: iii in beatus quoque apostolus iii epistula sua posuit looks damaged for in; glossed as in his letter

last_rejected.quote: so he must delight in us
last_rejected.source_quote: sic sibi placeat et ille de nobis
last_rejected.why: Purpose clause: our conduct should make the Father pleased with us. English makes his delight an obligation.
last_rejected.fix: As we delight in God as Father, so may he also delight in us.
last_rejected.ruling: "sic sibi placeat et ille de nobis" is a jussive subjunctive ('so may he be pleased with us'); 'must delight' is slightly strong but conveys the sense without changing the meaning.
